title: Maximum Peaks at Minimum Cost
src: Walmart OA, IIT Guwahati (2026). Coding question.
body:
You are given an array t of n integers. An index i is a peak if t[i-1] < t[i] and t[i] > t[i+1]. The first and last indices can never be peaks.

In one operation you may add any positive value to any element. You want the array to end up with the largest possible number of peaks, while the total value added is as small as possible.

Return that minimum total value added.

Function to complete

Complete minCostPeaks(t). It returns the minimum total value added.

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.
out: One integer: the minimum total value added.

samples.ex: At most 2 peaks are possible. Adding 2 at index 2 and 2 at index 4 gives [5, 1, 4, 3, 6, 5], where 4 and 6 are peaks. Total added: 4.
Only index 1 can be a peak. It must exceed both neighbours (1), so add 1.

wrong.why: always uses indices 1, 3, 5, ... (wrong when n is even and a shifted pattern is cheaper)
only tries the all-odd and all-even index patterns, never a mix
